hints: Think about how tissue fluid is made at the arteriole end of the capillary, what is squeezed out through the tiny gaps by high hydrostatic pressure?
Remember the size rule: water, ions and small molecules pass out very easily, phagocytes can squeeze out by diapedesis, and small plasma proteins can also escape in small amounts.
walkthrough:
**Recall how tissue fluid forms**

Think of tissue fluid as filtered blood plasma. At the arteriole end, high blood pressure forces fluid out through gaps in the capillary endothelium.

So anything small enough, or able to squeeze through, can leave the blood.

**Check each component by size and movement**

Sodium ions ($Na^+$) are tiny solutes, so they pass out freely with water and glucose. Phagocytes are white blood cells that can squeeze between endothelial cells to patrol tissues. Small proteins can also leak out in low concentrations, even though most large plasma proteins stay in the blood.

**Match to the table**

That means all three, phagocytes, proteins and sodium ions, are present in tissue fluid. That is row A with tick, tick, tick.

options.A: Correct. Sodium ions pass out freely, phagocytes leave by squeezing out, and small amounts of protein are also present in tissue fluid.
options.B: Incorrect. It correctly includes phagocytes but wrongly says proteins and sodium ions are absent, when both do enter tissue fluid.
options.C: Incorrect. It correctly includes proteins and sodium ions but wrongly says phagocytes are absent, when they do move into tissues to fight pathogens.
options.D: Incorrect. It correctly includes proteins but wrongly excludes phagocytes and sodium ions, both of which are found in tissue fluid.
